prd.name: alder
prd.provenance: Consolidates the original RFC (notes1), the extension/dependency addendum (notes2), three review rounds that corrected the composition algebra, error model, data-role hierarchy, numerical-backend boundary, cross-fitting module boundary, and refit compatibility, the reviewed Scala 3.7.4 baseline amendment, and the reviewed application-layer and experiment-lifecycle amendment.

review.evidence: docs/reviews/prd-2026-07-25.md, docs/reviews/scala-3.7.4-amendment-2026-07-26.md, and docs/reviews/application-dsl-amendment-2026-07-26.md; the superseding canonical PRD SHA-256 and implementation issue graph are recorded in mote.
corrections: FeatureMap.crossFitted is implemented in alder-data as an extension on FeatureMap.type, beside the Resampler protocol and implementations; alder-kernel never depends on alder-data.
FoldEncoder.fit preserves the caller's U <: Use.Fit role so cross-fitted refit workflows do not require an illicit Refit-to-Train retag.
Seed-allocation associativity is a Transform-composition law, not a Pipe law.
ArtifactCodec uses immutable IArray[Byte] payloads so the immutable-artifact contract is not undermined by mutable array aliases.
Scala 3.7.4 is the publication baseline; Alder 0.1 deliberately does not promise that Scala 3.3.x consumers can read its TASTy.

Cross-fitting requires CompleteResampler, whose assessment partitions cover every input row exactly once; rolling-origin remains an evaluation-only Resampler because its initial analysis window is never assessed.

FoldEncoder states are Trained and encode failures retain Failure stage provenance; FoldEncoder.andThen exposes analysis-row encode failures in its FitError union. FeatureMap rowwise postprocessing is total mapOutput in 0.1 rather than an unaudited arbitrary fitted Pipe.
The application layer is a staged construction and lifecycle facade over the existing algebra, never a fourth component protocol or an alternative pipeline interpreter.
The contract now requires non-empty validation and train-validation-test split results, closing the gap between the roles produced by alder-data and the roles consumed by EvaluationSources.

The contract now requires specialized evaluation to produce Scored observations and metric results before validation selection; role-typed evaluation and selection receipts preserve the exact plan, data, metric, and role evidence.

Split fractions are exact reduced rationals with fixed total-N apportionment; RankV1 fixes membership, duplicate source RowIds fail before receipt construction, and Experiment derives the sole split seed from its root schedule.
Experiment retains route and exact metric capability through every shared state, uses explicit selection policy, and expands every transition into the existing core algebra.
ObjectiveMetric owns its direction and score audit encoding, while every Metric retains unconditional CommutativeMonoid, partition, and permutation laws.
Base alder-application never depends on alder-tune or reconstructs a tuning family; the caller supplies the concrete learner reconstructed from Study selection.
Plan fingerprints are policy-tagged like every other fingerprint, and experiment phase seeds are derived by stable domain separation rather than traversal order.
Tuning erases model capabilities only: trial evaluation failures remain typed rather than being reduced to display strings.
implementationGates: Implement and law-test exact split apportionment, RankV1 allocation, duplicate-RowId rejection, non-empty validation and train-validation-test results, the precommitted Train/Test evaluation source, specialized Scored evaluation, lawful metric accumulators and identity, selection receipts, and receipt-gated refit before presenting Experiment as complete.

Implement Blueprint as exact typed wrappers around concrete Transform, FeatureMap, FoldEncoder, and Learner values; no application-layer operation may introduce a runtime stage registry, widened error channel, or second semantics.
Implement the synchronous Experiment runner and its phase-error ADT before quickstart presets; effectful execution must interpret the same state machine without unsafe execution.
The first executable guide, compile-negative diagnostics, compatibility checks, and JVM, Scala.js, and Scala Native gates must pass before the application layer is considered release-ready.

vision.thesis: An Alder program is an immutable value that may be fitted only on data marked for fitting, and that produces an immutable, audited, typed function from an input X to a prediction P. For preprocessing, fitting also produces the exact transformed training observations that may safely be passed to the next stage — and the type system tracks who may consume them.
vision.centralContribution: Prepared: a fitted artifact plus leakage-safe training rows, governed by a preparation-scope discipline. Target-independent preparation is reusable; cross-fitted target-dependent preparation is terminally consumable; anything beyond that requires explicit whole-chain cross-fitting. No mainstream framework names this distinction.
vision.governingPrinciple: The compiler rejects category errors, laws test semantic obligations, and runtime validation handles data-dependent facts. No layer pretends to do another layer's job.
audience: Application authors composing preprocessing and models into leakage-safe workflows
Third-party model authors: new ML models target Alder's three unfitted traits as THE interface
Coding agents implementing models against a small, explicit, law-checked SPI

designPrinciples.name: Restraint rule
designPrinciples.rule: A type parameter belongs in the public API only when changing it changes which programs are legal.

designPrinciples.name: Lawfulness over convenience
designPrinciples.rule: The safe API only states laws that are actually true. Where the industry-standard shortcut violates a law (e.g. pooled-OOF standardization), Alder refuses to certify it, offers a lawful alternative at similar cost, and reserves the shortcut for the explicitly unstable SPI where no law is claimed.
designPrinciples.framing: The restriction is about lawfulness, not a claim of large practical bias. Second-order leakage through pooled statistics is real but O(1/n) for smooth statistics; docs must not overstate its magnitude.

designPrinciples.name: No universal estimator
designPrinciples.rule: There is no Estimator base class, no isFitted, no clone protocol, no reflective parameter maps, no runtime capability tags, no metadata routing. Unfitted values simply lack prediction operations; capabilities are typeclass evidence; metadata requirements are context bounds (WeightOf[M], GroupOf[M], TimeOf[M]).

designPrinciples.name: Fitted artifacts never travel without their audit
designPrinciples.rule: Trained[A] pairs the artifact with a mandatory Audit. Audit construction is framework-owned via FitContext; plugins supply only identity, version, validated config, and backend fingerprint.

designPrinciples.name: Alder owns statistics, not linear algebra
designPrinciples.rule: Alder owns statistical algorithms and small fused loops (Welford moments, standardization). It owns no general-purpose linear-algebra kernel. Gale is the preferred numerical implementation substrate behind optional adapters — never Alder's public ontology of what a matrix is.

designPrinciples.name: The library carries its own proofs
designPrinciples.rule: Approachability and type discipline are not opposite ends of a slider. Application authors name consequential data, policy, backend, identity, and ownership decisions; Alder infers or encapsulates evidence that its values already contain. The goal is fewer visible annotations, not fewer guarantees.
reviewTest: Preserve a type when it prevents a real category error, but improve its constructor, inference boundary, staged operation, or diagnostic.
Infer or encapsulate proof bookkeeping that only transports evidence between Alder components.
Expose policy as an explicit named and auditable preset with an escape hatch; never as ambient mutable configuration.
ergonomicObligations: Progressive disclosure uses one algebra: simple and advanced programs differ only in the decisions they make visible.
Every convenience operation has one canonical expansion into existing primitives and preserves exact values, types, failures, plan identity, stage order, seeds, audit lineage, and finalization.
Composability is tested by naming, passing, conditionally extending, reusing, and repeatedly executing a program; example line count is a signal, not a soundness override.
Compiler diagnostics are public interface. An ordinary invalid program reports the caller's field, stage, role, or policy before internal match types or implicit-search machinery.
Exact overloads and extensions are preferred to broad implicit conversions. Syntax quotas never justify casts, ambient inference, stringly builders, or a second algebra.
Convenience may hide completed ownership but never an unresolved resource or protocol scope.

buildAndCompatibility.rationale: Alder publishes and tests from one current Scala baseline across its platform matrix. Scala 3.7.4 can consume the 3.3.8 TASTy published by Gale and linop4s; the reverse is not promised, so Alder 0.1 consumers and plugin authors must use a compiler capable of reading 3.7.4 TASTy. This compatibility tradeoff is explicit rather than hidden behind an untested cross-minor promise.

ci.required: Scala 3.7.4 on JVM and Scala.js; Scala Native is additionally required for kernel and laws
ci.advisory: future Scala versions (continue-on-error); Scala Native for pure modules beyond kernel and laws

compatibilityGates.mima: from the first published release (0.1), not deferred
compatibilityGates.evolutionPolicy: New functionality arrives via extension methods, final helper classes, and capability typeclasses — never by adding abstract members to frozen traits.

compilerFlags.note: Source-quality policy for Alder's own build only; never a consumer requirement. -Yexplicit-nulls may be relaxed in Java-interop-heavy backend modules.

kernelDependencies.rationale: One stable Cats dependency beats a bespoke miniature Cats hidden inside an ML framework (EitherT, Eq, monoids, law interop).

dataDependencies.rationale: alder-data interprets Tessera's zero-dependency ordinal plans; tessera-designs is a test-only integration dependency and is not on Alder's published runtime graph.

buildAndCompatibility.crossBuild: Pure modules (kernel, laws, data, preprocess, metrics, tune, models-linear, application, and quickstart) cross-build JVM + Scala.js + Scala Native from day one — Native CI is the forcing function that keeps the kernel platform-clean (required for kernel+laws, advisory for the rest). Backend adapters follow their libraries: alder-ridge-linop4s all three platforms, alder-ridge-gale JVM + JS.

rules: Ordinary fitting accepts NonEmptyData[U, A] for U <: Use.Fit.
Tuning accepts only NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A]; no overload accepts evaluation data.
No public asTrain / retag / unsafePromote. Promotion happens through narrow audited constructors only.

refitProtocol.afterTuning: A Study Selection chooses a configuration but grants no data-role authority. The concrete family(selection.best) may fit the original Train data directly. Adding Validation observations requires a successful typed validation selection receipt and receipt-gated Refit promotion.
refitProtocol.afterValidation: An alder-application extension on Refit.type accepts SelectionReceipt and consumes its data-owned private PromotionAuthority[Use.Validation] to produce NonEmptyData[Use.Refit, Example[X, Y, M]] containing exactly train+validation. alder-data never names SelectionReceipt. A raw EvaluationReceipt[Use.Validation] proves completed validation scoring but cannot authorize promotion.
refitProtocol.afterFinalEvaluation: An alder-application extension accepts EvaluationReceipt[Use.Test] and consumes its data-owned private PromotionAuthority[Use.Test] to promote exactly the receipt's all-observed manifest: train+test after a precommitted holdout, or train+validation+test after a selected refit and final test.
refitProtocol.auditObligation: Every refit audit records its ordered sources, the authorizing evaluation and selection identities where applicable, and the explicit claim that the refitted artifact has not itself been evaluated on the held-out role that authorized it.
refitProtocol.noShortcut: No split object exposes refitTrainAndValidation or another direct retag. A role-typed evaluation receipt proves that every held-out row was predicted and scored. Only a SelectionReceipt may authorize adding Validation data; only an EvaluationReceipt[Use.Test] may authorize the exact all-observed manifest for deployment refit.

constructors: Split.holdout(data, spec, seed) — a precommitted train/test evaluation with no model-selection claim
Split.validation(data, spec, seed) — train plus validation for fitting, scoring, and explicit selection
Split.trainValidationTest(data, spec, seed) — the complete selection, refit, and final-test lifecycle
splitVocabulary.sizes: HoldoutSpec, ValidationSpec, and TrainValidationTestSpec contain checked Rows or Fraction policies but no seed. Rows is a positive Long. Fraction is a reduced exact rational numerator/denominator with 0 < numerator < denominator; binary floating-point is not its semantic representation. Literal and dynamic constructor spelling is provisional, but every constructor has these exact semantics.
splitVocabulary.apportionment: For source size N, a two-way Fraction assigns floor(N * numerator / denominator) rows to its held-out role and the remainder to Train. A three-way specification computes Validation and Test counts independently against the same total N, in that order, and assigns the remainder to Train; its exact rational validation+test sum must be < 1. Rows specifications use their stated held-out counts against total N. Multiplication and comparison are overflow-safe. If any resulting role has zero rows or held-out counts exhaust N, splitting returns a typed EmptySplitRole or ExhaustiveSplit error rather than clamping, rounding up, or silently changing policy.
splitVocabulary.seedAuthority: The core Split constructors require one explicit seed. Direct-core callers supply it. Experiment stores only an unseeded route-compatible specification, derives the split-phase seed from its root schedule, and passes that seed to the same constructor. No application constructor accepts both a root seed and an independently chosen split seed.
splitVocabulary.nonEmpty: Every partition produced by a successful public split is NonEmptyData. Split construction already proves nonemptiness, so callers are never required to transport that proof again.
splitVocabulary.algorithm: SplitAlgorithm.RankV1 first validates every fingerprint-policy and digest text field under the byte contract below, then rejects a duplicate source RowId with DataError.DuplicateSourceRow(id), and only then computes ranks. Two-way splitting assigns the lowest held-out-count ranks to the held-out role. Three-way splitting assigns the lowest Validation count to Validation, the next Test count to Test, and the remainder to Train. Each role is then restored to original source order. This is one total disjoint assignment, not two split calls.

rankV1Encoding.frame: text(s) = u32be(length(utf8(s))) || utf8(s). Inputs must be well-formed Unicode scalar sequences; an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate fails validation, and no Unicode normalization is applied. The length is the UTF-8 byte count, not character count; u32be is exactly four unsigned big-endian bytes. Text longer than 2^32-1 bytes is not encodable and fails validation.
rankV1Encoding.domain: The first field is text("alder.split.rank-v1"), whose payload bytes are exactly 61 6c 64 65 72 2e 73 70 6c 69 74 2e 72 61 6e 6b 2d 76 31.
rankV1Encoding.input: bytes = text("alder.split.rank-v1") || encoded fingerprint policy || text(fingerprint.digest) || i64be(seed.value) || i64be(rowId.value). i64be is the exact eight-byte big-endian two's-complement representation of the signed Long.
rankV1Encoding.fnv1a64: Starting h = 0xcbf29ce484222325, for each input byte b interpreted unsigned set h = ((h xor b) * 0x00000100000001b3) mod 2^64.
rankV1Encoding.integerSemantics: All arithmetic is modulo 2^64 and >>> is logical right shift. Rank order interprets the final 64 bits as a signed two's-complement Long; equal ranks are ordered by signed RowId.
rankV1Encoding.goldenMembership: For ContentDigest("sha256"), digest "abc", seed 0, and source-order RowIds [0,1,2,3,4], signed rank order is [1,4,2,0,3]. Holdout Rows(2) yields Train [0,2,3] and Test [1,4]. Three-way Validation Rows(1), Test Rows(2) yields Train [0,3], Validation [1], and Test [2,4], with each role shown in restored source order.

rankTextErrors: enum RankTextField: ContentDigestAlgorithm | SourceIdentityUri | SourceIdentityVersion | SummaryPolicyId | FingerprintDigest
enum RankTextError: UnpairedSurrogate(codeUnitIndex: Int) | Utf8LengthExceedsU32(byteLength: Long)
splitVocabulary.receipt: SplitReceipt records the source fingerprint, split policy fingerprint, explicit seed, ordered role fingerprints, and role counts. Production receipts contain no RowId lists; testkit evidence checks exact membership.
splitVocabulary.policyFingerprint: The split policy fingerprint commits to RankV1, exact reduced fractions or row counts, role order, apportionment rule, and hash/framing versions. A different allocation algorithm or rounding rule is a different policy and fingerprint.
laws: Every input RowId appears in exactly one output role; no row is lost or duplicated.
Equal source identity, rows, split policy, and seed produce equal membership, role order, fingerprints, and receipt.
Malformed or oversized RankV1 text returns InvalidRankText naming the field and reason; it is never normalized, replaced, thrown, or widened.
A duplicate source RowId fails before membership, role fingerprints, or a SplitReceipt is produced.
Fraction and Rows apportionment follows the fixed total-N rule on boundary-sized and adversarial inputs.
Role values cannot be publicly constructed, retagged, or exchanged.
Changing a meaningful split parameter changes the policy fingerprint even when a small dataset happens to receive the same membership.

evaluationSources.validation: EvaluationSources.validation(train, validation) validates nonempty held-out data, RowId disjointness, and a Train+Validation manifest.
evaluationSources.precommittedTest: EvaluationSources.precommittedTest(train, test) is data-owned and validates nonempty held-out data, RowId disjointness, and a Train+Test manifest. It requires a precommitted Holdout path and does not pretend that Train has a validation-refit audit.
evaluationSources.finalTest: EvaluationSources.finalTest(refit, test) requires the prior receipt-authorized Train+Validation refit audit, validates the untouched Test partition, and produces the Train+Validation+Test manifest.
evaluationSources.construction: All constructors are role-specific and return typed RefitError values. alder-application calls them but cannot manufacture EvaluationSources or alter their observed-source manifests.

data.rowIdentity: Every logical row carries a stable internal RowId supporting split-disjointness checks, out-of-fold reconstruction in original order, leakage tracing in law tests, and auditable fold lineage.

accessSpi.semanticPath: def foldRows[B](initial: B)(step: (B, RowId, A) => B): B
hotPaths: def foreachBatch(size: BatchSize)(step: RowBatch[A] => Unit): Unit
trait RowBatch[+A] { def length: Int; def rowId(index: Int): RowId; def value(index: Int): A }
accessSpi.rationale: foldRows alone allocates per row; batched access must exist before the SPI is frozen.

observations: final case class Example[+X, +Y, +M](input: X, target: Y, meta: M)
final case class Scored[+Y, +P, +M](truth: Y, prediction: P, meta: M)
data.metadataCapabilities: M is real application data, never Map[String, Any]. Requirements are typeclasses visible in signatures: WeightOf[M], GroupOf[M] { type Key }, TimeOf[M]. A grouped resampler requires GroupOf; rolling-origin requires TimeOf; weighted learners/metrics require WeightOf. There is no metadata router.

schemas.applicationSchemas: Case classes and enums, e.g. final case class House(...) derives Schema, Coordinates, CanEqual

definition: def writeTo(value: A, destination: CoordinateWriter): Either[CoordinateError, Unit]
rules: Derivation succeeds only for complete numeric products; Option[Double] fields do not derive — imputation must first produce a complete type.
None, null, NaN, and 'missing' are never treated as interchangeable.
writeTo is the non-allocating hot path (e.g. straight into a gale DMatBuilder or an operator workspace).

schemas.dynamicVectors: Dense[S] / Sparse[S] carry a runtime schema fingerprint plus a semantic phantom feature-space brand S. Learned dimensions are validated runtime values, never type-level naturals. Sparse[S] is not public in 0.1.

sparsePreprocessingPolicy.problem: Mean-centering densifies sparse data: per-row, (x − μ) makes structural zeros nonzero. sklearn handles this with a runtime error (with_mean=True on sparse input); Alder makes the invalid state unrepresentable instead.
rules: Sparsity-preserving preprocessing exists as Sparse[S] => Sparse[S] transforms (scale-only standardization: x ⊙ invStd keeps zeros zero; the config ADT for the sparse scaler simply has no centering case).

Representation changes are explicit, auditable transforms: Densify[S]: Transform[F, Sparse[S], Dense[S]] (and Sparsify where lawful). A user who wants centered sparse data must say so in the plan, and the cost appears in the plan fingerprint.

Centering that a MODEL needs (e.g. ridge's unpenalized intercept) is not a preprocessing stage at all — it is backend-owned algebra, already specified: gale adapters use means-correction formulas without materializing centered data; linop4s composes the rank-one update X − 1μᵀ as a lazy operator, which is exactly what its inspectable expression tree is for.
Serving is unaffected either way: a Pipe densifying one row at a time is cheap; the hazard is only fit-time materialization of n dense rows.
sparsePreprocessingPolicy.court: Alder owns the type-level policy, the explicit-densification ergonomics, and the laws (scale-only preserves the sparsity pattern; densification never happens implicitly). Backends own centering-by-algebra when a model policy requires it. gale owns efficient sparse value-array operations.

definition: final def andThen[E2, C](next: Pipe[B, E2, C]): Pipe[A, E | E2, C]
final def mapError[E2](f: E => E2): Pipe[A, E2, B]
pipe.decision: Error is a covariant type parameter, not a refinement-type member. Explicit parameters compose with unions naturally and are mechanically easier for plugin authors and coding agents than Pipe[X, Z] { type Error = E } bounds.

definition: final case class Failure[+E] private[alder] (stage: StagePath, cause: E):
failure.rationale: A naked E1 | E2 cannot say which stage failed when stages share an error type. The union is the cause type; Failure carries provenance. StagePath is allocated from the normalized logical plan, not runtime Chain nesting, so parenthesization changes neither stage identities, seed derivations, nor first-failure paths.

errorModel.fitResult: type FitResult[F[_], E, A] = EitherT[F, Failure[E], A]
errorModel.unionSemantics: Scala 3 unions are associative and commutative ((A | (B | C)) =:= ((A | B) | C)), so the cause set is parenthesization-invariant. Fit errors remain associated type members (chosen once per implementation); combinators expose unions (left.FitError | right.FitError). Applications collapse growing unions deliberately via mapFitError/mapRunError — information loss is explicit, never automatic.
errorModel.replayErrors: Because Transform.fit owns its training replay, replay failure surfaces inside that transform's FitError (e.g. case ReplayFailed(error: RunError)). Transform.andThen(Transform) FitError is exactly left.FitError | right.FitError. Other combinators that must execute a fitted component over training rows expose that component's RunError explicitly in their FitError union; protocol/alignment validation uses the typed PreparationError channel. No fit-time execution failure is hidden or discarded.

preparationScopes.note: Reusable extends LearnerReady (corrected from sibling design): target-independent preparation is a fortiori safe for a terminal learner, so covariance grants LearnerReady consumption for free; the extra privilege (feeding another fitted stage) remains Reusable-only.

semantics.Reusable: No target information was used. Rows may feed another Transform, a FeatureMap, or a Learner.
semantics.LearnerReady: Each row was prepared without its own target (cross-fitted). Rows may feed a terminal Learner only; feeding another preprocessing stage requires whole-chain cross-fitting.

definition: final class Prepared[+S <: Preparation, +U <: Use.Fit, +A, +B] private[alder] (
rules: rows is a protocol resource, not a collection: it is not publicly extractable. Sanctioned combinators inside Alder consume it; summaries/receipts/lineage are publicly inspectable.

The Reusable factory takes only the fitted pipe plus the fitting data and PERFORMS THE REPLAY ITSELF — the input-only replay law is true by construction and cannot be violated by a third party. Score-reuse optimizations (e.g. PCA scores materialized during fit) live in alder.unsafe.spi where the law suite polices them.
FeatureMap's LearnerReady rows are deliberately NOT required to equal replaying the final fitted pipe.

transform.role: Target-blind preprocessing. Cannot inspect Y or M because they do not occur in its input.
definition: def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, X])(using FitContext)
: FitResult[F, FitError, Prepared[Preparation.Reusable, U, Fitted, Z]]
transform.correction: fit returns Prepared (not merely Trained): Transform ∘ Transform needs the first stage's prepared rows, and the replay that produces them can fail — each stage owns its replay and its replay errors.

definition: trait FeatureMap[F[_], X, Y, M, Z]:
def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext)
: FitResult[F, FitError, Prepared[Scope, U, Fitted, Example[Z, Y, M]]]

safeConstructors.inputOnly: FeatureMap.inputOnly(transform) — lifts a Transform; library preserves targets, metadata, row identities; result scope is Reusable.
safeConstructors.crossFitted: FeatureMap.crossFitted(encoder: FoldEncoder, resampler: CompleteResampler) — provided by alder-data as an extension on FeatureMap.type, beside the Resampler protocol, so the kernel/data dependency remains one-way. CompleteResampler certifies that assessment partitions cover every input RowId exactly once; KFold and grouped KFold qualify, rolling-origin does not. TesseraResampler.complete admits only Plan[Split[Selection], Coverage.ExactOnce]; Holdout, Bootstrap, and repeated exact plans are rejected statically, so the adapter performs no runtime coverage check. The constructor owns the protocol: split; fit each analysis partition; encode only its held-out assessment partition; reassemble OOF rows in original order; fit one final serving state on all rows; record both lineages. Analysis and assessment remain protocol partitions of the original Fit role: assessment rows are encoded, never passed to a fitting signature, so retagging them as Use.Test would erase the parent Train/Refit role and is neither necessary nor sound. There is deliberately no safe convenience constructor for encoder.fit(all).encode(all).

definition: trait FoldEncoder[F[_], X, Y, M, Z]:
def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext): FitResult[F, FitError, Trained[State]]
def encode(state: State, input: X): Either[Failure[RunError], Z]

composition.law: FoldEncoder[F, X, Y, M, Z] ∘ Transform[F, Z, W] = FoldEncoder[F, X, Y, M, W] (encoder.andThen(transform))
composition.semantics: The inner transform is fitted per-fold on analysis rows only — whole-chain cross-fitting for the two-stage case, true by construction, at the cost of k+1 inner fits instead of 1.
composition.errors: The composed FitError is encoder.FitError | encoder.RunError | transform.FitError because encoder output must be computed on analysis rows before fitting the transform. State is Trained and child audits are retained. encode keeps Failure stage provenance from both stages.
composition.motivation: Restores the flagship pattern (target-encode then standardize then learn) inside the safe API, which the composition table otherwise outlaws: crossFitted(targetEncoder.andThen(standardizer), folds).learnWith(lr). REQUIRED for 0.1.

learner.role: Terminal learning algorithm. May depend on all training targets because its in-sample predictions are not passed downstream.
definition: trait Learner[F[_], X, Y, M, P]:
def fit[U <: Use.Fit](data: NonEmptyData[U, Example[X, Y, M]])(using FitContext)
learner.terminality: Feeding a model's in-sample predictions into a second learner is the wrong protocol; calibration/stacking/distillation go through explicit CrossFit.predictions(baseWorkflow, folds).learnWith(calibrator). Pure prediction postprocessing stays easy: trained.mapPrediction(Decision.argmax).

abstractions.serving: Effectful/remote/native inference is compiled separately: trait Serving[F[_], -X, +P] { type Error; def predict(input: X): F[Either[Error, P]] }. Local Pipe inference is pure.
abstractions.trained: final class Trained[+A] private[alder] (val artifact: A, val audit: Audit). Constructed only via FitContext.complete.

compositionAlgebra.decision: There is no Workflow trait. 'Workflow' is a descriptive word for a composed Learner. Composition closes over the three unfitted abstractions.

lawfulCompositions.note: the function has no fitted state or training dependency; preparation scope is preserved
inner transform fitted per-fold on analysis rows; the 0.1 route to target-encode-then-standardize

lawfulCompositions.why: second-order leakage: pooled statistics fitted on OOF rows reintroduce own-target dependence through other rows

leakageModel.rowwiseLaw: row r was not used directly to fit the state producing row r — NECESSARY BUT INSUFFICIENT
leakageModel.transitiveLaw: r ∉ transitiveTargetDependencies(outputFor(r)) — the target of row r must be absent from the entire dependency closure of the representation produced for r
leakageModel.counterexample: Encoder folds A={1,2}, B={3,4}. z3, z4 were fitted using y1, y2. A target-blind standardizer fit on pooled OOF rows has μ depending on y1 through z3, z4; therefore (z1 − μ)/σ depends on y1 despite the standardizer never inspecting a target.
leakageModel.magnitudeHonesty: The dependence is O(1/n) for smooth pooled statistics; pooled-OOF standardization is universal practice in sklearn/mlr3/tidymodels. Alder's docs frame the restriction as lawfulness (the rowwise law is simply false there), not as a claim of material bias.
leakageModel.learnerExemption: The terminal learner may depend on all targets; the moment its predictions feed calibration or stacking, the entire preceding chain must again be cross-fitted.

futureWork.wholeChainCrossFitting: CrossFit.whole(first, second, outer) / first.nestedWith(second, outer): for every outer fold, fit the entire preceding pipeline (including inner cross-fitting) on outer analysis rows; fit downstream preprocessing inside that analysis set; apply only to outer assessment rows; reassemble in original order; fit one serving chain on all data. DEFERRED past 0.1 — one target-aware preprocessing boundary per ordinary workflow is the principled initial restriction; FoldEncoder.andThen covers the common case.

compositionAlgebra.combinatorObligations: Combinators (ThenTransform, LearnedWith, ...) know nothing algorithm-specific. They own: preparation scope, row identity, audit composition, child FitContexts (context.forChild(ordinal)), error widening, lineage. Seeds derive from root seed + normalized plan fingerprint + stable stage ordinal; parenthesization must not change stage seeds, audit paths, or fitted behavior.

applicationLayer.status: Ratified semantic contract with deliberately provisional source spelling. Blueprint, Experiment, exact desugaring, lifecycle states, and error-preservation obligations are fixed; wrapper class names, method names, and artifact names remain provisional until compile-iteration confirms inference and diagnostics.
applicationLayer.role: The application layer is an optional entrance to Alder's existing component and evaluation algebra. It constructs concrete composed Learner values and executes the existing split, fit, evaluation, metric, selection, and refit protocols. It defines no fourth component trait, runtime pipeline representation, plugin interface, or alternative semantics.

moduleBoundary.generic: Provisional artifact alder-application: pure JVM/Scala.js/Scala Native module depending on alder-kernel, alder-data, and alder-metrics. It owns Blueprint, Experiment, scored evaluation integration, and application-facing lifecycle results.
moduleBoundary.batteries: Provisional artifact alder-quickstart: optional pure module depending on alder-application, alder-preprocess, alder-models-linear, and alder-ridge-linop4s. It owns the curated prelude, supervised Unit-metadata constructors, checked split-size syntax, and named standardize/ridge presets.
moduleBoundary.evaluationOwnership: alder-data owns role-typed partitions, EvaluationSources, AllObserved, PredictionResult, PredictionReceipt, and private role-typed PromotionAuthority without depending on metrics. alder-application combines those values with Metric to construct ScoredEvaluation, role-typed EvaluationReceipt, SelectionReceipt, and extensions on Refit.type that consume the private authority. alder-data never names an application-layer type. This keeps the dependency direction alder-kernel -> alder-data/alder-metrics -> alder-application.
moduleBoundary.dependencyRule: Neither module is a dependency of alder-kernel, alder-data, alder-metrics, or a component plugin. Third-party Transform, FeatureMap, FoldEncoder, and Learner implementations work unchanged. Metric is not yet a frozen 0.1 SPI; metric implementations adopt the ratified descriptor contract before publication.
moduleBoundary.oneAlgebra: Application values always expose their exact underlying core value. Advanced callers may leave the facade at any completed construction boundary without conversion, serialization, reinterpretation, or loss of type information.

fixed: Blueprint is staged construction over exact core values and a completed Blueprint exposes one concrete Learner.
Experiment is the typed owner of split, candidate fit, validation scoring, selection, refit, final test, and optional deployment refit.
ExperimentFailure retains exact component FitError and RunError causes plus explicit lifecycle phase.
Validation and train-validation-test split roles, scored evaluation, selection evidence, and receipt-gated refit are public semantic contracts.
provisional: The alder-application and alder-quickstart artifact and package names.
The concrete state-wrapper names and the spelling of via, withFeatureMap, crossFit, insideFolds, mapOutput, learn, score, select, and run.
Rows/Fraction smart-constructor syntax and exact names of curated model presets.
apiStability.freezeRule: Provisional spelling becomes public only after positive composition fixtures, compile-negative fixtures, diagnostic snapshots, Scaladoc, and all three platform builds pass. Compile iteration may simplify spelling but may not weaken the fixed semantic contract.

blueprint.definition: A Blueprint state is a final typed wrapper with a stable val whose value has the concrete component type T, FM, or L. Associated members remain available through that stable term — for example state.transform.FitError and complete.learner.Model — rather than through erased Scala 3 type projections or match-type recovery from T, FM, or L. A FoldEncoder remains concrete while crossFit immediately expands it through FeatureMap.crossFitted. No state stores a trait-typed stage list. The wrapper itself performs no fit and consumes no data; it delegates construction to existing combinators.

states.contains: Input, target, and metadata type intent only; synchronous quickstart entry points infer F = cats.Id and M = Unit without displaying either.
A stable val transform: T containing the exact T <: Transform[F, X, Z]; transform.FitError, transform.RunError, and transform.Fitted remain term-dependent members.
allows: append one FeatureMap or cross-fitted FoldEncoder boundary
forbids: erasing T to Transform[F, X, Z]

states.contains: A stable val featureMap: FM containing the exact FM <: FeatureMap[F, X, Y, M, Z]; featureMap.Scope, featureMap.FitError, featureMap.RunError, and featureMap.Fitted remain term-dependent members.
forbids: a fitted Transform after target-aware preparation

states.contains: A stable val learner: L containing the exact L <: Learner[F, X, Y, M, P]. Associated members remain available as learner.Model, learner.FitError, and learner.RunError.
allows: pass the learner to core Fit
name, reuse, or conditionally choose the completed value

canonicalExpansions: Empty.withFeatureMap(fm) contains fm; TargetBlind(t).withFeatureMap(fm) contains t.andThen(fm).
Empty.crossFit(e, r) contains FeatureMap.crossFitted(e, r); TargetBlind(t).crossFit(e, r) contains t.andThen(FeatureMap.crossFitted(e, r)).

Target-aware postprocessing is constructed inside the fold boundary: crossFit(e.insideFolds(t), r) expands to FeatureMap.crossFitted(e.andThen(t), r). It never expands to crossFitted(e, r).andThen(t).
Empty.learn(l) contains l; TargetBlind(t).learn(l) contains t.learnWith(l); LearnerReady(fm).learn(l) contains fm.learnWith(l).
blueprint.equivalence: For every expansion, the facade and direct-core values have equal precise result types and are observationally equal for fitted model behavior, prepared-row behavior where observable to laws, first failure cause and StagePath, normalized stage order, phase and child seeds, audit children, preparation lineage, component descriptors, and refit audit. A wrapper contributes no audit node, stage ordinal, fingerprint input, or seed.
blueprint.compositionUsability: A completed or intermediate Blueprint can be assigned to a val, returned from a function, selected conditionally when branch types agree, extended by another legal operation, and reused for repeated fits. The API is not accepted merely because one inline demo is short.
banned: Vector[Any], List[Stage], reflective registries, string stage names as execution keys, or an interpreter over a new pipeline AST
trait-typed fields that erase concrete associated errors or model types
automatic mapFitError or mapRunError to String, Throwable, Any, or a universal application error
broad implicit conversions from arbitrary values into components, expressions, configs, or Blueprint states
a facade-only composition that has no lawful core expansion

experiment.definition: Experiment is a typed state machine over one completed Blueprint, an explicit route R <: ExperimentRoute, an identified non-empty Data[Use.Unsplit, Example[...]], one root Seed, a route-compatible unseeded split specification, a stable exact learner value, a stable exact metric value, and an explicit selection policy where selection occurs. The state notation below omits carried F, X, Y, M, prediction, and metric-result parameters for readability; implementations retain them and use stable-term dependent members rather than erased type projections. Reporting-only Metric values may complete evaluation, but only the retained ObjectiveMetric value may authorize selection. Private constructors and route-constrained methods ensure states arise only from successful legal transitions.
experiment.routeStorage: The implementation may use route-specific final state classes or a private application-owned associated mapping from R to its Spec and split result. Callers never provide route evidence, inspect a public match type, or pattern-match an erased union to recover the partition. Diagnostics name Validation, TrainValidationTest, or PrecommittedHoldout directly.
states: Defined[R, L, Mt, S] — stable vals learner: L and metric: Mt, validated plan and source identities, policy-tagged PlanFingerprint, root Seed, identified NonEmptyData[Use.Unsplit, Example[...]], and the unseeded split specification fixed for R.

Partitioned[R, L, Mt, S] — the exact route-specific Holdout, ValidationSplit, or TrainValidationTestSplit produced with the framework-derived split-phase seed; the original unsplit source is no longer an execution choice.
CandidateFitted[R, L, Mt, S] — retains R, learner, metric, split, and Trained[learner.Model] fitted on the split's Use.Train data; no validation or test authority has been consumed.

Validated[R <: ValidationCapableRoute, L, Mt, S] — retains R and the exact metric Mt, plus non-empty scored validation observations, exact score S, EvaluationReceipt[Use.Validation], and AllObserved(train+validation).

Selected[R <: ValidationCapableRoute, L, Mt, S] — exists only when the retained Mt is an ObjectiveMetric; it holds a framework-owned SelectionReceipt binding plan, validation evaluation, metric, score, and selection policy.

Refitted[R <: ValidationCapableRoute, L, Mt, S] — the same stable learner fitted on receipt-authorized Use.Refit train+validation data. Its audit states that the new artifact has not itself been evaluated on the authorizing Validation; for TrainValidationTestRoute it also proves that no Test access preceded this fit.

Tested[L, Mt, S] — arises only from Refitted[TrainValidationTestRoute, ...] and contains the selected refitted model scored by the retained metric on non-empty Use.Test data, EvaluationReceipt[Use.Test], and AllObserved(train+validation+test).
PrecommittedTested[L, Mt, S] — a plan fixed before held-out access, fitted on Holdout.train, then scored by the retained metric on Holdout.test without a validation-selection claim.

DeploymentRefitted[L, Prior] — optional learner.Model fitted on all observed labelled data after either tested route; Prior retains the exact selected or precommitted test report, and the audit states that this new deployment artifact has not itself been evaluated on the authorizing Test.

routes.validation: Defined[ValidationRoute, ...] partitions its unsplit source with ValidationSpec, then permits Partitioned -> CandidateFitted -> Validated. An ObjectiveMetric additionally permits Selected and an explicit optional selected refit. No state on this route has a test method or makes an unbiased final-test claim.
routes.trainValidationTest: Defined[TrainValidationTestRoute, ...] partitions once with TrainValidationTestSpec, then permits Partitioned -> CandidateFitted -> Validated -> Selected -> Refitted -> Tested. Selection requires the retained ObjectiveMetric. Test is inaccessible before Refitted.
routes.precommittedHoldout: Defined[PrecommittedHoldoutRoute, ...] partitions its unsplit source with HoldoutSpec, then permits Partitioned -> CandidateFitted -> PrecommittedTested and optional DeploymentRefitted. It exposes no validation, selection, or selected-refit method and cannot be relabelled as another route.
routes.tuning: A Study may choose a config inside Use.Train. Model capability erasure remains confined to Study. The caller reconstructs family(selection.best), completes the concrete Blueprint, and supplies that exact learner to base Experiment. alder-application does not depend on alder-tune or reconstruct a tuning family. A future convenience integration, if needed, belongs in a separate one-way adapter depending on both modules. Any later addition of Validation rows still requires the ordinary validation evaluation and application selection receipt.

canonicalTransitions: Defined.partition derives SeedSchedule.split(root, plan), then calls exactly one matching core constructor: Split.holdout(source, spec, seed), Split.validation(source, spec, seed), or Split.trainValidationTest(source, spec, seed). It adds no second allocation or membership policy.

Partitioned.fitCandidate calls the retained learner's ordinary fit protocol on the exact split.train with the candidate-fit phase FitContext. CandidateFitted stores the returned Trained value without widening learner.Model, learner.FitError, or learner.RunError.

CandidateFitted.validate builds EvaluationSources.validation(split.train, split.validation) and calls Evaluation.scored with the retained metric. The precommitted route instead calls data-owned EvaluationSources.precommittedTest(split.train, split.test) and passes that value to the same scored evaluator.

Validated.select is available only for a retained ObjectiveMetric. It calls that metric's direction and auditScore, applies the explicit SelectionPolicy, and constructs SelectionReceipt from the exact validation EvaluationReceipt and private authority; it neither fits nor retags data.

Selected.refit consumes the application-owned SelectionReceipt through the narrow Refit extension, producing exactly train+validation Use.Refit data, then invokes the same learner under the selected-refit phase FitContext.
Refitted.test builds EvaluationSources.finalTest from the receipt-authorized Use.Refit data and the untouched Test partition, then calls Evaluation.scored with the retained metric.

Tested.deploymentRefit and PrecommittedTested.deploymentRefit consume only their exact Test EvaluationReceipt through the narrow Refit extension, produce all-observed Use.Refit data, and call the same learner under the deployment-refit phase FitContext.

Each route-specific complete runner is exactly the corresponding sequence above. It contributes no alternative split, fit, evaluation, selection, promotion, fingerprint, seed, audit, or error semantics.

definition: def scored[U <: Use.Evaluation, X, Y, M, RunE, P0, S, Mt <: Metric[Scored[Y, P0, M], S], P <: Pipe[X, RunE, P0]](
): Either[ScoredEvaluationError[RunE], ScoredEvaluation[U, X, Y, M, P0, S]]
scoredEvaluation.specialization: The implementation predicts from Example.input, preserves truth and metadata, and produces NonEmptyData[U, Scored[Y, P0, M]] plus exact S.
scoredEvaluation.result: ScoredEvaluation[U, X, Y, M, P0, S] contains scored observations, score, metric descriptor, EvaluationReceipt[U], all observed source data, and the split/evaluation fingerprints. It does not stringify P0, S, RunE, or MetricError.
scoredEvaluation.streaming: Metric accumulation folds the role-typed Data directly under the Metric partition law. No public Vector materialization is required.
scoredEvaluation.atomicity: Generic prediction may return PredictionResult and PredictionReceipt after every held-out RowId succeeds, but those values grant no refit authority. EvaluationReceipt[U] is emitted only after the declared metric finishes successfully. Selection and refit authority therefore cannot arise from partial prediction or failed scoring.

selection.receipt: SelectionReceipt[L, Mt, S] is framework-constructed and retains the stable exact learner and ObjectiveMetric values while binding their policy-tagged PlanFingerprint, validation EvaluationReceiptId, source and scored-data fingerprints, MetricDescriptor, exact score S, metric-owned auditable score value, direction, and selection policy.
selection.singleCandidate: Selecting the only candidate is an explicit select(SingleCandidate) decision because it authorizes later access to Validation rows for refit. The validation convenience stops at Validated and never applies this policy implicitly. SingleCandidate is a named policy value rather than a proof witness assembled by the caller.
selection.candidateBoundary: Base Experiment contains one exact learner and performs no multi-candidate search. Multiple candidates belong to Study, whose deterministic tie policy and complete trial history remain in StudyAudit. Experiment may receive the concrete learner reconstructed from Study.selection.best, but it does not reinterpret the candidate set.
selection.authority: The public receipt identifier is reproducible evidence; private authority links the selected state to the exact AllObserved bundle and underlying EvaluationReceipt[Use.Validation]. Identifiers alone cannot mint Refit data.

rules: Each case constructor identifies the broad lifecycle phase. DataPhase, SplitPhase, FitPhase, EvaluationPhase, SelectionPhase, and RefitPhase distinguish source validation, route split, candidate fit, validation/test evaluation, selection, selected promotion, selected refit, deployment promotion, and deployment refit where those distinctions affect recovery.
Failure retains the exact leaf cause and StagePath. ExperimentFailure adds lifecycle phase rather than replacing component provenance.
Expected failures are never thrown, converted to display strings, hidden in Option, or widened to Throwable or Any.
Human rendering is an extension at the application edge and cannot be used as the program's error contract.

identityAndSeeds.plan: PlanFingerprint is policy-tagged. Experiment requires an explicit stable identity or an explicitly supplied fingerprint; it never guesses from a display name, class name, toString, hashCode, runtime stage list, or source location.
identityAndSeeds.data: Application constructors require an explicit DataFingerprint or an explicitly tagged external identity. They do not claim to compute a content digest unless a declared digest policy actually reads the relevant content.
identityAndSeeds.phaseSchedule: One root Seed is deterministically domain-separated by policy-tagged plan fingerprint and stable phase tag: split, candidate-fit, validation-protocol, selected-refit, test-protocol, and deployment-refit. Component child seeds then derive from the phase fit seed and normalized stage ordinal.
identityAndSeeds.splitAuthority: Experiment accepts an unseeded HoldoutSpec, ValidationSpec, or TrainValidationTestSpec. It derives the only split seed from the split phase and passes it to the public core Split constructor. Direct-core use still supplies its seed explicitly.
identityAndSeeds.stability: Adding logging, changing wrapper allocation, traversing a collection differently, or reparenthesizing a Blueprint cannot change membership or seeds. The exact schedule is public testkit vocabulary and part of facade/core equivalence.
identityAndSeeds.backend: Experiment never summons or chooses a numerical backend. The completed learner already contains an explicitly constructed backend or named preset, and its ComponentDescriptor and BackendFingerprint remain authoritative.

executionBoundary.sync: The primary 0.1 onboarding methods execute cats.Id components and return Either[ExperimentFailure[experiment.learner.FitError, experiment.learner.RunError], ExactTerminalState] without requiring callers to name Id, EitherT, Monad, or Cats syntax.
executionBoundary.completeMethods: Distinct route-constrained methods have exact terminal types: validation reporting ends at Validated, validation selection ends at Selected, explicit validation refit ends at Refitted, train-validation-test ends at Tested, and precommitted holdout ends at PrecommittedTested. Deployment refit is a separate operation. There is no single generic runner whose result depends on a runtime optional-refit flag.
executionBoundary.effectful: Core components remain effect-polymorphic. An effectful Experiment interpreter sequences the identical state transitions in F with an explicit lawful capability; it does not hardcode IO, call unsafeRunSync, or introduce a second lifecycle.
executionBoundary.scope: Synchronous execution is required for the first application slice. The general effectful interpreter may follow after the synchronous state machine and equivalence laws are stable.

quickstart.prelude: One curated import exposes application constructors, checked split specifications, built-in metrics, standardization, ridge presets, and result accessors. It does not re-export every Alder implementation type.
quickstart.data: Supervised.fromPairs or its final spelling constructs Example[X, Y, Unit] without making callers write Unit; explicit fromRows/fromExamples variants preserve metadata and weighted workflows. Every constructor still requires honest source identity.
presets: A standardize preset expands to the existing StandardScaler with an explicit zero-variance policy.
A ridgeLsqr preset expands to validated RidgeConfig, RidgeRegression, and Linop4sRidgeBackend.lsqr. The engine name is visible in the constructor and backend audit.
There is no unnamed ambient ridge backend. Gale and other engines use separate named presets with their actual configuration and platform support.
quickstart.validation: Dynamic invalid values return typed constructor errors. Literal-oriented syntax may reject invalid constants at compile time, but syntax targets never justify throws, casts, or broad implicit conversions.
quickstart.escapeHatch: Every preset exposes or documents its exact generic expansion, and users may substitute any compatible Transform, FeatureMap, FoldEncoder, Learner, Metric, or backend value.

usabilityContract.firstWorkflow: The executable getting-started guide must construct identified supervised data, declare a ValidationSpec, build standardize plus named LSQR ridge, provide one root seed from which Experiment derives the split seed, fit, predict every validation row, compute a real metric, and stop at a typed Validated result. It must create no unused Test partition and must not silently select or refit the candidate.
usabilityContract.budget: Target one import and roughly twelve non-data lines for the first successful workflow. This is a regression signal, not a mandate: it cannot override explicit identity, meaningful policy, sound ownership, or useful diagnostics.
visibleDecisions: explicit selection policy when validation authorizes refit
usabilityContract.diagnostics: Compile-negative fixtures cover illegal post-target fitting, a second target-aware boundary, fit on Evaluation data, scoring before fit, selected-route test before selected refit, a test method on ValidationRoute, selection with a reporting-only Metric, and missing metadata capabilities. Runtime-negative tests cover same-role receipt substitution and one-shot receipt reuse, including concurrent attempts, because Scala does not provide affine values. The first diagnostic or typed runtime error names the role, stage, receipt, field, or missing capability in application language.
verification: Facade and direct-core programs are observationally equal.
First failure stage and lifecycle phase are both preserved.
All convenience values remain nameable, passable, conditionally extensible, reusable, and repeatedly executable.
JVM, Scala.js, and Scala Native tests, mdoc, Scaladoc snippets, compatibility checks, and the rendered site pass on Scala 3.7.4.

predictionSemantics.rule: Prediction semantics are the result type, never a string mode. Typical: Double, Distribution[Class], Class, Ranking[Item], SurvivalCurve[Time], Quantiles[Probability, Double], Gaussian.
predictionSemantics.decisions: A probabilistic classifier is Learner[F, X, Class, M, Distribution[Class]]; a hard decision is a separate pure pipe (Decision.argmax). Metrics get honest input types: LogLoss requires Distribution[C]; Accuracy requires C. Mixing them without an explicit decision rule does not compile.
predictionSemantics.semanticValues: Distribution, Probability, Positive, NonNegative, PositiveInt etc. are opaque types with controlled constructors: dynamic values return typed validation results; literal constructors validate at compile time (NonNegative.const(-0.1) does not compile).

definition: trait ObjectiveMetric[-A, S] extends Metric[A, S]:
metrics.descriptor: MetricDescriptor contains a stable metric id, version, validated parameters, reproducible numeric policy, and, for an ObjectiveMetric, the objective direction and score-encoding version. ObjectiveMetric is invariant in S because it consumes S when producing audit evidence. Direction and auditScore are owned by the same stable metric value whose descriptor enters the receipt; a broad or locally substituted encoder cannot change receipt identity behind an unchanged metric descriptor.
rules: Evaluation streams/parallelizes without changing the public metric (partition law).

Every Metric accumulator is a lawful CommutativeMonoid and every built-in numerical Metric uses a reproducible mergeable representation. The public partition and permutation laws are unconditional for Metric.

An order- or partition-sensitive fast accumulator is not a Metric and cannot be passed to generic Evaluation. If introduced after 0.1, it uses a separately typed sequential or ordered SPI with visibly weaker execution semantics; a numeric-mode flag cannot retract CommutativeMonoid laws.
Weighted metrics are different values with different requirements (weightedRmse[M: WeightOf]), never optional arguments.
Built-in RMSE and accuracy values expose ObjectiveMetric with Minimize and Maximize respectively and own the canonical audit encoding for their branded result types.
A metric result used only for reporting needs no ordering. A selection API cannot accept a reporting-only Metric or invent an objective direction.
Metric identity, parameters, direction, exact result, and auditable score value are retained by ScoredEvaluation and SelectionReceipt.

space.rule: Space[A] is applicative, not monadic: every emitted value is a complete, valid A. No tune()/unknown() sentinels; no partially valid configs. Conditional structure is an explicit sum type (enum TreeShape). Data-dependent spaces are ordinary functions FeatureSchema => Space[A].

erasure.rule: Path-dependent Model types are kept (they power ArtifactCodec[learner.Model], Explain, PrincipalComponents on stable values). Tuning erases them deliberately at the boundary via eraseModel — named to say capabilities are being discarded — producing LearnerView[F, X, Y, M, FitE, RunE, P] with Trained[Pipe[X, RunE, P]].

study.rule: A Study[F, C, A, E] accepts training data only (NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A]); no overload accepts evaluation data. It returns Selection[C, E](best config, every typed trial, StudyAudit) — a selected configuration, not an existentially typed fitted artifact. TrialFailure[E] retains the evaluation cause E alongside NonFiniteObjective; no study or application layer reduces candidate failures to description strings. The concrete family(selection.best) may fit the original Train data directly. Adding validation observations requires the ordinary validation receipt and Refit protocol, retaining the stable learner's path-dependent Model.
definitions: final case class Trial[C, +E](config: C, objective: Either[TrialFailure[E], Double])
final class Selection[C, +E] private[tune] (val best: C, val trials: Vector[Trial[C, E]], val audit: StudyAudit)
final class Study[F[_], C, A, E] private (..., evaluate: (C, NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A]) => F[Either[TrialFailure[E], Double]])
def run(data: NonEmptyData[Use.Train, A]): F[Either[StudyError[E], Selection[C, E]]]
rules: The same E appears in TrialFailure, every Trial, Selection history, StudyError, the evaluation callback, and run; there is no unbound or existential error parameter.
NonFiniteObjective widens from TrialFailure[Nothing] without inventing an E.
Study uses the shared ObjectiveDirection vocabulary from alder-metrics and records direction, deterministic tie policy, candidate order, seed, and completion counts in StudyAudit.

fingerprints.rule: Every value named Fingerprint records the policy that produced it. ContentDigest, SourceIdentity, and Summary are never interchangeable, even when their rendered digest strings match.
fingerprints.plan: PlanFingerprint is a final policy-tagged value, not an opaque bare String. PlanFingerprint.external(identity) records Summary(alder.external-plan-identity); a canonical descriptor digest records its real content algorithm. Seed derivation hashes both policy and digest with a stable cross-platform encoding.
fingerprints.application: Experiment requires explicit plan and data identity. Display names may accompany those identities but cannot silently become content-digest claims.

rules: Part of the result of fitting, not an experiment-tracker side channel.
Raw data need not be embedded; the fingerprinting policy (digest, source identity, privacy-preserving summary) must itself be recorded.

Cross-fitted lineage is a compact plan receipt: policy-tagged resampler fingerprint, seed, policy-tagged assignment digest, ordered per-fold analysis/assessment fingerprints plus fitted-state lineage, and final all-row serving lineage. Production lineage never embeds RowId lists.

Application-level SplitReceipt, ScoredEvaluation, and SelectionReceipt remain separate typed protocol evidence. RefitAudit records the exact receipt identities that authorized a promoted dataset and the resulting unevaluated-artifact claim.

fitContext.definition: final class FitContext private[alder] — a final framework-owned class, NEVER a trait. Third parties consume it, never implement it; final classes gain compatible methods without breaking plugins.
fitContext.completeProtocol: context.complete(artifact, trainedOn, component: ComponentDescriptor) constructs Trained[A]. The framework supplies stage path, data fingerprint, root/derived seeds, numeric mode, parent lineage, schema fingerprint, child audits. The plugin supplies only ComponentDescriptor(id, version, validated parameters as AuditValue, backend fingerprint). Plugins cannot omit framework-level provenance.

solverReceipt.rationale: Alder-owned neutral schema. linop4s Termination/SolveResult/Evidence map into it (Constructed/NumericallyChecked/UserAsserted -> AssumptionEvidence.*); the original library value may ride in an adapter-specific extension. Optional backends never enter the kernel's audit schema.

provenance.determinism: Given equal actual ordered rows and RowIds, equal component values and policies, equal policy-tagged plan and data fingerprints, root seed, phase tag, backend fingerprint, and deterministic numeric mode, each experiment transition is observationally repeatable. A SourceIdentity or Summary fingerprint scopes an audit claim but does not prove that externally managed content stayed equal. Phase seeds use stable domain separation; component seeds use the normalized stage ordinal. Nondeterministic backends must say so in NumericMode.

capabilities.rule: A model exposes only typed prediction. Everything else is typeclass evidence: ArtifactCodec[A], Explain[A, X], Incremental[L], PrincipalComponents[A], InverseTransform[A]. Missing evidence means the operation does not compile — there is no runtime 'unsupported'. ArtifactCodec encodes and decodes immutable IArray[Byte] payloads; mutable Array aliases are not part of the public artifact contract.
codecLaws: decode(encode(model)).predict(x) == model.predict(x) for all valid x; audit round-trips without semantic loss.
Chain codec: ArtifactCodec derivation for Pipe.Chain given codecs of the parts — REQUIRED, or no composed workflow can ever be saved.
Java serialization is not an artifact format.

numericalBackends.boundaryRule: A third-party component pays for: the protocol + the numeric representation it actually uses + the solver it explicitly selects. Nothing else.

backendNeutrality.rule: Solver interfaces consume Alder-owned views (typed data + Coordinates, batched rows, CoordinateWriter), never a Gale matrix. Gale's DMat/DVec must not become Alder's interchange types: that would leak Gale's JDK 21 floor into every plugin and force the linop4s backend through a Gale representation.

gale.role: Preferred numerical implementation substrate (dense QR/Cholesky/LU, sparse, spectral, optional Vector-API/FFM-BLAS acceleration), behind adapter artifacts only.
gale.facts: Scala 3.3.8, JVM+JS, gale-core has zero compile-scope third-party dependencies, JDK 21 floor (22+ for FFM modules), own law suites, Breeze differential parity tests.

ridgeStrategies.NormalCholesky: solve (XᵀX + λI) β = Xᵀy — faster; squares the condition number; gale detects A.t * A structurally (syrk path) and addToDiagonal supplies λI

gale.intercept: Unpenalized intercept via centring: centre X and y, solve for coefficients, reconstruct intercept = mean(y) − mean(X)ᵀ β.
gale.backendCapture: The gale Backend given MUST be captured as a constructor field and fingerprinted at construction (GaleRidgeBackend(galeBackend, strategy, numericMode)). Never summon an ambient Backend inside solve — otherwise BackendFingerprint and the determinism law lie. Fingerprint includes gale version, backend report, native provider, thread config, strategy, numeric mode, centring/weighting policies, tolerances.
gale.gaps: Gale has no statistics (no colMeans/variance) and no elementwise vector algebra (no Hadamard, no vector division). Alder owns Welford/pairwise moments and standardization loops over IArray[Double] / CoordinateWriter.
gale.releasePrerequisite: Gale is 1.0.0-SNAPSHOT, unpublished, with inconsistent coordinates (io.github.canardlapin in build vs io.gale in docs). Sequence: settle org → cut gale 1.0.0 → add compat gates → pin Alder → publish alder-ridge-gale. publishLocal/source-dependency during development only; no stable Alder release depends on a snapshot.

linop4s.role: Genuinely independent second backend (matrix-free LinearMap/AdjointOp + Krylov: CG, MINRES, LSQR) and the stress test proving the backend boundary works.
linop4s.facts: Scala 3.3.8, JVM+JS+Native, core depends on cats-core + algebra only, capability types (PositiveDefinite etc.) with evidence, pure step-machine solvers, rich Termination ADT.

ridgeMapping.lsqr: Damped LSQR minimizes ||Ax−b||² + damp²||x||², so damp = sqrt(λ), NOT λ. Intercept handled by centring so it is not damped.
ridgeMapping.cg: PositiveDefinite.normalEquation(operator, λ) is a sound capability route; the audit must disclose normal-equation conditioning consequences.

linop4s.independence: gale and linop4s have no relationship to each other and Alder must not force one. Two separate adapter artifacts double as the proof of backend neutrality.
linop4s.agreementValue: Agreement between Gale QR/Cholesky and linop4s LSQR/CG is far stronger law-suite evidence than agreement between two wrappers over the same solver.
