openDecisions.question: Whether fallible or pre-fitted rowwise postprocessing should be admitted after defining FitContext stage rebasing, audit composition, and a training-independence receipt. The 0.1 safe surface is total FeatureMap.mapOutput only.

decisionLog.decision: Publish from Scala 3.7.4; advisory CI on future Scala versions.
decisionLog.rationale: A single current baseline keeps Alder's compiler and platform evidence coherent. Scala 3.7.4 reads the 3.3.8 TASTy of Gale and linop4s; Alder deliberately does not promise that 3.3.x consumers can read Alder 0.1 artifacts.

decisionLog.decision: Pipe error is a covariant type parameter; FitError/RunError stay associated members on unfitted traits; unions compose; Failure[E] carries StagePath.
decisionLog.rationale: Refinement-type bounds are hostile to plugin authors and agents; naked unions lose stage provenance.

decisionLog.decision: No Workflow execution or extension abstraction; composition closes over Transform/FeatureMap/Learner and the executable value is a composed Learner. Blueprint is an optional construction facade whose Complete state contains that exact concrete Learner; Experiment interprets the existing data/evaluation lifecycle around it.
decisionLog.rationale: The core stays small, terminality and exact associated types are preserved, plugins implement one protocol, and application authors gain progressive disclosure without a second pipeline representation or semantics.

decisionLog.decision: Adopt the transitive leakage law; FeatureMap∘Transform and FeatureMap∘FeatureMap are excluded from the safe API; Preparation scopes with Reusable <: LearnerReady.
decisionLog.rationale: Pooled statistics on OOF rows reintroduce own-target dependence through other rows; the rowwise law is insufficient. Reusable is strictly stronger, hence a subtype.

decisionLog.decision: Transform.fit returns Prepared and owns its training replay; the safe Reusable factory performs the replay itself.
decisionLog.rationale: Replay can fail (surfaces in FitError); by-construction replay makes the replay law unviolable; score-reuse goes to unsafe SPI.

decisionLog.decision: FoldEncoder.andThen(transform) ships in 0.1.
decisionLog.rationale: Restores target-encode→standardize→learn lawfully (per-fold inner fits are whole-chain cross-fitting for the two-stage case); without it the algebra outlaws the flagship example.

decisionLog.decision: Gale is the implementation substrate behind adapter artifacts; backends consume Alder-owned views, never DMat; gale Backend captured and fingerprinted at construction.
decisionLog.rationale: Prevents JDK-floor leakage, keeps linop4s genuinely independent, keeps determinism claims honest.

decisionLog.decision: linop4s is the second ridge backend (damped LSQR with damp=sqrt(λ), CG via PositiveDefinite.normalEquation); its ADTs map into an Alder-owned SolverReceipt.
decisionLog.rationale: Structurally different implementation makes backend-agreement laws meaningful; optional libraries must not enter the kernel audit schema.

decisionLog.decision: Use.Fit supertype with Train and Refit; refit via audited receipt-gated constructors; tuning accepts Train only.
decisionLog.rationale: 'No retagging ever' was too absolute; deployment refitting is standard and must be explicit, audited, and honest about unevaluated refits.

decisionLog.decision: Tuning erases via eraseModel to LearnerView; Selection returns the winning config; final refit retains the concrete path-dependent Model.
decisionLog.rationale: Uniform types where iteration needs them; capability-bearing concrete types everywhere else.

decisionLog.decision: FitContext is a final framework-owned class with a public constrained complete(...) factory.
decisionLog.rationale: Third parties consume, never implement; final classes evolve compatibly; framework provenance cannot be omitted (corrects notes1's Trained.internal).

decisionLog.decision: Data SPI includes foldRows plus foreachRow/foreachBatch and Coordinates.writeTo before freezing.
decisionLog.rationale: Per-row boxed folds cannot be the only path through the hot loop of every fit.

decisionLog.decision: All Alder artifacts (and the sparse-PCA reference plugin) publish under io.github.canardlapin; gale's docs are corrected to match its build (io.github.canardlapin), no vanity domain.
decisionLog.rationale: io.github groups verify on Sonatype in minutes; cross-org Maven dependencies are normal; a future org.typelevel migration would be a coordinate break at a major boundary regardless. Resolves O1.

decisionLog.decision: Single RidgeBackend taking a RowWeights ADT (Uniform | ByRow — a first-class case, never an absent optional); paired learner values with WeightedRidgeRegression requiring WeightOf[M].
decisionLog.rationale: Learner-side pre-scaling would rebuild scaled X through Coordinates.build (allocation plus 'scaled House' semantics); backends apply sqrt-weights where it is free (gale during DMatBuilder materialization, linop4s as a diagonal operator). Type-level evidence stays at the learner, mirroring the metric design. Weighted cases enter the backend-agreement laws, catching weighted-centring divergence. Resolves O2.

decisionLog.decision: PreparationLineage: three binding commitments now — (1) plan-shaped and per-fold in production audits (fold membership as resampler fingerprint + seed + assignment digest; per-row RowId lists only in the instrumented testkit), (2) every fingerprint carries its policy tag (ContentDigest(algo) | SourceIdentity(uri, version) | Summary(policyId)), (3) Audit/lineage types are final classes with accessors, not case classes. Full schema deferred to crossFitted implementation (O6).
decisionLog.rationale: Per-row lineage in production is a size and privacy hazard; final classes on the frozen surface can gain fields compatibly where case classes cannot. Resolves O3.

decisionLog.decision: Pure modules cross-build JVM + JS + Native from day one (Native required in CI for kernel+laws, advisory elsewhere); backend adapters follow their libraries.
decisionLog.rationale: Dependencies are cats-only and linop4s proves the 3.3.8 Native toolchain; removing a platform is a break while continuous Native CI is the forcing function that keeps the kernel platform-clean; yields a working Native ridge path via the linop4s backend. Resolves O4.

decisionLog.decision: FoldEncoder.andThen admits chains, with a coherence law: encoder.andThen(t1).andThen(t2) is observationally equal to encoder.andThen(t1.andThen(t2)), including stage paths and seeds.
decisionLog.rationale: Transform composition is already closed, so forbidding chains would be an unenforceable syntactic distinction; implementation is identical (fit the composed transform per fold). Linear k+1 cost per appended stage is documented and recorded in lineage. Prepending needs no FoldEncoder support: Transform ∘ FeatureMap is already lawful. Resolves O5.

decisionLog.decision: Sparse preprocessing: no centering constructor exists for Sparse[S] => Sparse[S] transforms (scale-only preserves sparsity); representation changes are explicit audited Densify/Sparsify transforms; model-required centering (ridge intercept) is backend-owned algebra (gale means-correction, linop4s rank-one operator X − 1μᵀ), never a preprocessing stage.
decisionLog.rationale: Turns sklearn's runtime error (with_mean on sparse) into a compile-time absence; fit-time densification becomes impossible silently and visible when chosen; the backend boundary already owned intercept centring, so the sparse case falls out of the existing design. See dataProtocol.schemas.sparsePreprocessingPolicy.

decisionLog.decision: Resampler is split into an evaluation protocol and CompleteResampler, which certifies exactly-once assessment coverage of every input RowId. FeatureMap.crossFitted accepts CompleteResampler only; KFold and grouped KFold qualify, rolling-origin does not.
decisionLog.rationale: Cross-fitting must reconstruct one OOF value for every input row. Rolling-origin leaves its initial analysis window unassessed, so accepting an undifferentiated resampler would make the required output impossible or invite an in-sample fill-in. The capability changes which programs are legal and therefore belongs in the type system under P1.

decisionLog.decision: FeatureMap has an associated Scope <: Preparation.LearnerReady so inputOnly and mapOutput retain Reusable statically. FoldEncoder.fit returns Trained[State], encode returns Either[Failure[RunError], Z], and FoldEncoder.andThen exposes encoder.RunError in its FitError union. FeatureMap rowwise postprocessing in 0.1 is total mapOutput, not an arbitrary bare or pre-fitted Pipe.
decisionLog.rationale: Preparation scope changes which downstream programs are legal and cannot be erased by the base trait. Encoder state is fitted state and cannot travel without audit under P4. Per-fold downstream fitting executes encoder output on analysis rows, so those run failures are real fit failures and must remain typed. Stripping Failure.cause would delete stage provenance. A bare Pipe violates mandatory audit, while a Trained Pipe still lacks proof it was independent of the prepared rows; total mapOutput has no training dependency and preserves scope honestly.

decisionLog.decision: Cross-fitted PreparationLineage stores a compact plan receipt: a policy-tagged resampler fingerprint, the split seed, a policy-tagged assignment digest, ordered fold receipts containing fold index plus analysis/assessment fingerprints and fitted-state lineage, and the final all-row serving-state lineage. A Tessera-backed plan additionally retains an Alder-owned rendering of the complete Tessera verification receipt (design algorithm, digest algorithm, design/population/labels/assignment fingerprints, and plan seed). No production field contains RowIds.
decisionLog.rationale: This is sufficient to reproduce and audit which plan produced every OOF partition without turning production audits into row-level privacy and size liabilities. Explicit fold receipts keep the structure plan-shaped, while the assignment digest commits to exact membership. The dependency-neutral receipt rendering preserves Tessera's policy tags without making alder-kernel depend on tessera-core. Resolves O6.

decisionLog.decision: Published law artifacts follow ownership dependencies: alder-laws covers alder-kernel contracts; alder-metrics-laws depends on alder-metrics; alder-tune-laws depends on alder-tune plus the core laws/testkit.
decisionLog.rationale: A kernel-only alder-laws artifact cannot compile laws for Metric or Space because those types are owned by downstream modules. Making downstream implementations depend on a law artifact that itself requires their types creates a module and tracker cycle. Separate law artifacts preserve one-way dependencies and consumer opt-in test scope.

decisionLog.decision: alder-data may depend on tessera-core and interprets Plan[Split[Selection], Coverage.ExactOnce] through a total CompleteResampler factory. tessera-designs is test-only. The adapter binds Tessera ordinals to Alder RowIds, maps GroupOf metadata to canonical Labels, converts seeds, and retains policy-tagged receipt fields. Runtime checks are limited to binding compatibility (population size, population fingerprint, and seed), never coverage.
decisionLog.rationale: The integration spike found that Coverage.Exact is exact once per repeat, while Alder cross-fitting requires exactly once over the entire plan. A repeated K-fold therefore cannot lawfully mint CompleteResampler. Tessera's stronger ExactOnce proof closes that gap and makes Holdout, Bootstrap, and repeated plans compile-negative while preserving runtime validation for facts that depend on the later Alder data value.

decisionLog.decision: Adopt P6: the library carries proof bookkeeping while callers retain meaningful data, policy, backend, identity, and ownership decisions. Convenience uses progressive disclosure over one algebra and must have an exact canonical expansion.
decisionLog.rationale: Type discipline and approachability conflict only when callers restate evidence Alder already possesses. Exact expansion and facade/core laws remove ceremony without deleting guarantees or creating a simple API with different semantics.

decisionLog.decision: Add checked unseeded split specifications, exact rational total-N apportionment, duplicate-RowId rejection, deterministic RankV1 allocation, and non-empty ValidationSplit and TrainValidationTestSplit with SplitReceipt. Add role-specific EvaluationSources.precommittedTest for the existing Train+Test Holdout path. Generic prediction emits only role-typed coverage evidence; specialized evaluation converts held-out Example rows to Scored rows and finishes a typed Metric before emitting EvaluationReceipt. Validation refit requires SelectionReceipt; Test EvaluationReceipt may authorize only its exact all-observed manifest for deployment refit.
decisionLog.rationale: The existing Holdout produced Train plus Test while EvaluationSources offered only Validation and post-validation final Test construction, leaving both getting-started validation and honest precommitted holdout scoring incomplete. Exact apportionment and versioned ranking prevent platform or implementation choice from changing a receipt behind one policy. Separating prediction coverage, completed evaluation, and selection prevents a partially completed validation path from acquiring broader data authority. Split construction already proves nonemptiness, so its return types carry that proof.

decisionLog.decision: Experiment is a private-constructor typed state machine whose shared states retain route, stable learner, and exact metric capability through partition, candidate fit, validation score, selection, receipt-gated refit, final test, and optional deployment refit. Each transition has one canonical expansion into existing core operations. ExperimentFailure adds lifecycle phase while retaining exact stable-term learner errors and Failure stage attribution.
decisionLog.rationale: A short runner is honest only if it performs the same core split, fit, evaluation, selection, and promotion operations. Retaining route and metric evidence prevents a validation-only state from acquiring a test method or a reporting metric from acquiring selection authority. Phase context and component context answer different questions and neither should erase the other.

decisionLog.decision: PlanFingerprint becomes policy-tagged; Experiment requires explicit plan and data identity, stores an unseeded route-specific SplitSpec, derives the sole split and later phase seeds by stable domain separation, and never chooses a backend. Named presets construct and audit a specific backend.
decisionLog.rationale: A display string, class name, hashCode, or ambient given cannot support reproducibility claims. A root seed plus an independently supplied split seed would create competing authorities. Phase separation prevents unrelated protocol changes from perturbing fitting randomness, while explicit backend-bearing presets keep convenience auditable.

decisionLog.decision: Metrics used for selection are stable ObjectiveMetric values that own their MetricDescriptor, objective direction, and canonical score audit encoding. Every Metric accumulator obeys unconditional CommutativeMonoid, partition, and permutation laws; order-sensitive fast accumulation requires a different future SPI. Tuning erases model capabilities only: TrialFailure retains its typed evaluation cause instead of a description String.
decisionLog.rationale: Selection receipts must say what was optimized and what failed without allowing a local encoder to change their meaning. A mode flag cannot retract a typeclass law. Model-type erasure is required for iteration; error erasure is not and would contradict Alder's explicit failure algebra.

decisionLog.decision: Ship the application contract in two optional pure cross-platform layers: a generic Blueprint/Experiment module and a curated quickstart module. Semantic names and laws are ratified; exact artifact, package, state-class, method, and smart-constructor spelling remains provisional until compile and diagnostic fixtures pass.
decisionLog.rationale: Separating generic lifecycle machinery from batteries avoids forcing ridge or preprocessing dependencies on every application. Delaying spelling freeze permits inference-driven refinement without reopening the safety contract.
